conviction_note: Q3 numbers are new and the company's own compiled consensus (NII 2,818m, net profit 1,634m) is the bar; a modest profit beat is likely (four straight beats, real-estate gains guided to continue, Q3 Euribor 12m average +23bp), but the CFO deferred any NII-guidance refinement to year-end results, and Spanish banks are selling in-line or better Q3 prints this fortnight (Bankinter -7.56%, Santander -5.6%, BBVA -2.6%). So the size is mid (4.5%) and the sign is a slight lean down (p_up 46). The findings sum (-0.7) and the scaled number (-0.36) agree in sign. Both are small because the fundamental read (+3% vs bar) and the reaction function point opposite ways.

already_public.what: Results date and time: webcast of Q3 2026 results on 30 Oct 2026 at 09:00 CET (OIR)

Company-compiled consensus as of 14 Oct 2026: 3Q26 NII 2,818m, services revenues 1,388m, recurring opex -1,687m, LLPs -249m, net profit 1,634m; FY26 NII 11,176m (11,326m in July), FY26 net profit 6,533m
Guidance reminder: FY26 NII >11bn, services revenues ~+5%, cost growth ~4.5%, CoR <0.25%. Kept unchanged at H1 (29 Jul), and the stock fell 7.1% that day

Key-updates pre-close note: CFO at the BofA conference (22 Sep) said loan growth is easing to ~7% or below, NII sensitivity is ~5%, and NII guidance will be reassessed at year-end results with the 2027 guide; Q3 average Euribor 12m 3.02% (+23bp QoQ); 92 days vs 91
Interim dividend range 30-40% of H1 profit (961-1,281m), to be paid in November and set in October
8th SBB (500m, max six months from 30 Apr) 68.01% executed (340.1m) as of 22 Oct

new_in_release.expect: NII around the 2,818m consensus (Euribor tailwind and an extra day against a lower sensitivity and a flatter curve); net profit modestly above 1,634m on fees, real-estate gains and benign CoR

FY26 NII '>11bn' most likely reiterated, or only tweaked toward consensus; the CFO deferred a formal refinement to year-end. No upgrade is the base case, and it was the July disappointment. Slight negative
Probable new SBB to follow the expiring 8th programme (500m already deducted from CET1, about 150m unexecuted), offset by the Cetelem bid. Mild positive, uncertain
Interim dividend set within the known 30-40% range; last year's was 0.1679 EUR (40%). Neutral unless it comes in below 40%
Commentary on deposit costs, mortgage slowdown and Cetelem M&A; unknown sign

bar: CaixaBank's own compiled consensus as of 14 Oct 2026 (min. 15 analysts): 3Q26 NII 2,818m, net profit 1,634m (https://www.caixabank.com/informacionparaaccionistaseinversores/informaciongeneral/analistas/consenso_en.html). Press consensus is lower: EFE 9M 4,792m implies Q3 ~1,589m (https://www.infobae.com/espana/agencias/2026/10/18/la-gran-banca-espanola-gana-cerca-de-29235-millones-de-euros-hasta-septiembre-un-15-mas/), and ON Economia has Q3 1,547m. The profit bar is disputed by 3-5%; the NII bar is single-sourced from the company
session_check: bmo. The issuer's OIR of 15 Sep 2026 sets the Q3 results webcast for 30 Oct 2026 at 09:00 CET, the Madrid open, and CaixaBank publishes its press release and financial report ahead of the webcast; on 29 Jul 2026 the H1 release traded the same session (-7.12% close to close). https://www.caixabank.com/StaticFiles/pdfs/260915_OIR_Webcast_es.pdf
positioning_check: Register not covered for this market: the CNMV short-position grid returns no rows from this container (positioning.covered false, anchor_covered false), so nothing is known about short interest and priced_lean_pct (+0.32) is the 20-day run-up. The only flow seen is the issuer's own SBB: about 10m EUR a week (877,581 shares, 16-22 Oct), roughly 2-3% of daily volume, ending around 30 Oct.

findings.finding: At the BofA conference on 22 Sep the CFO deferred any refinement of NII guidance to the year-end results and the 2027 guide, so the 30 Oct release will most likely reiterate the FY26 NII '>11bn' guide (consensus already 11,176m). That is the same non-upgrade the stock fell 7.1% on in July.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 29 Jul 2026: H1 beat, guidance unchanged, stock -7.12% (sector -1.1%). 30 Jan 2026: upgraded targets, +6.75%
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the statement is public in the issuer's own pre-close note, and the stock is -12.7% over 60 days. But Jefferies called the July non-upgrade a disappointment, and higher Euribor since then (Q3 12m average 3.02% vs 2.78% in Q2) invites hope of an upgrade. If no upgrade were fully expected, the July reaction would not have needed a rate leg to repeat.
findings.independence: AOL/Reuters on July: 'Caixabank keeps 2026-27 guidance unchanged, shares fall' https://www.aol.ca/articles/caixabanks-q2-net-profit-10-042709000.html

findings.finding: The Q3 NII drivers are disclosed by the issuer: average 12m Euribor 3.02% (+23bp QoQ), 3m 2.52% (+27bp), 92 days vs 91, and management called Q2 the trough. Company consensus NII of 2,818m (+3.3% QoQ) already embeds this, and peers printed in line (Sabadell NII +2% QoQ; Bankinter NII in line).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 NII 2,729m vs ~2,748-2,760m consensus (a small miss) on a -7.1% day
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the rate tape is public and consensus has absorbed it. FY26 NII consensus was cut from 11,326m to 11,176m since July, so the bar is not stretched. The only residual is whether the 'trough' call delivers above +3.3% QoQ.

findings.finding: Net profit is likely to beat the 1,634m company consensus modestly. CaixaBank beat EPS consensus four quarters running (+7% to +12%), Q2 profit was 1,631m vs 1,559m expected, and management guided continued positive real-estate disposal gains 'clearly above zero' plus a benign 24bp cost of risk.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This name sells its beats: the Q2 beat of +4.6% on profit went with -7.12%; the Q1 beat went with +1.69%
findings.original_quote: beneficio neto atribuido de 1.631 millones ... por encima del consenso (1.559 millones) [paraphrase of article figures]
findings.why_not_priced: A habitual beat is partly expected; the company consensus (1,634m) already sits above the press consensus (1,547-1,589m). Part of the beat would be gains on repossessed assets, which the market treats as lower quality.
findings.independence: Beat history in the baseline consensus block (Yahoo earningsHistory): surprises of +7.1%, +8.5%, +11.8% and +8.3% over the last four quarters

findings.finding: Spanish banks are being sold on in-line or better Q3 prints this fortnight: Bankinter -7.56% on 22 Oct ('a estos niveles el mercado no permite decepciones'; European banks -4.33%), Santander -5.6% on 28 Oct (Brazil), and BBVA down as much as 5% intraday on 29 Oct with Spain profit -0.2%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: CABK fell -5.8% on 22 Oct in sympathy with Bankinter and -7.12% on its own July print
findings.original_quote: Los analistas coinciden en que los resultados son buenos, pero a estos niveles el mercado no permite decepciones en algunas métricas, como las comisiones y el margen bruto.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a reaction function, not a fact about CaixaBank; CABK has already de-rated alongside its peers (-6.5% over 20 days), which absorbs part of it. If it were fully priced, the latest peer prints (BBVA today) would not still be falling on release.
findings.independence: Expansión market report, 29 Oct: 'El mayor castigo lo recibe ... BBVA. El banco sufre caídas de hasta el 5%' https://www.expansion.com/mercados/cronica-bolsa/2026/10/29/ibex-desbordado-referencias.html

findings.finding: The 8th SBB (500m, max six months from 30 Apr) was only 68.01% executed (340.1m) by 22 Oct and lapses around 30 Oct. The full 500m was already deducted from CET1 (-20bp), so a follow-on programme of at least the ~150m residual costs no new capital; the Q3 2025 release carried a 500m SBB. Offset: the pending Cetelem bid (~0.9-1.0bn).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 release with a new 500m SBB: +1.69%
findings.why_not_priced: The programme's expiry date and under-execution sit in weekly OIR filings that the wire does not aggregate. A follow-on is the norm and partly expected; the Cetelem pursuit (Expansión, 27 Oct) introduces doubt about its size.
findings.independence: 30 Apr 2026 inside information on the six-month duration and the -20bp CET1 deduction: https://www.caixabank.com/StaticFiles/pdfs/260430_IP_SBB_es.pdf

findings.finding: The forward volume and funding narrative is softening: the CFO guided loan growth easing from 8% to ~7% or below with less potential in mortgages, and deposit growth lower on a falling savings rate. UBS flags 250-300bn of near-zero-cost household deposits as a weak point as competition rises, and BBVA reports Spanish mortgage new production +2.1% YTD vs +22% a year earlier.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: none observed on this line specifically
findings.original_quote: Con unos depósitos de los hogares de entre 250.000 y 300.000 millones de euros que prácticamente no ofrecen remuneración alguna, es lógico que los inversores vean esto como un posible punto débil
findings.why_not_priced: Largely public via the BofA fireside chat and peer prints; the residual is whether Q3 shows deposit-cost or volume deceleration beyond what was said. Macro-to-company transmission is not yet confirmed in a CaixaBank number.
findings.independence: BBVA mortgage data: https://www.expansion.com/empresas/banca/2026/10/29/bbva-apuesta-ganar-cuota-empresas-consumo-frenazo-hipotecario.html; CFO comments in https://www.caixabank.com/deployedfiles/caixabank_com/Estaticos/PDFs/Accionistasinversores/Accion_Caixabank/Key_Updates.pdf

outside_window.finding: CaixaBank is the lead bidder for BNP Paribas Personal Finance (Cetelem) in Spain and Portugal, with EY on due diligence and Morgan Stanley advising; price ~0.9-1.0bn, target loss-making in H1, due diligence ends late Nov or early Dec. The call may mention it, but a decision lands after the window.
Formal 2027 NII guidance and the refinement of the 2026 guide are deferred to the FY26 results (January 2027), per the CFO at BofA on 22 Sep

baseline_tension: The findings lean slightly negative, while the baseline lean is +0.32 (the 20-day run-up of -6.48% read as mean reversion). The sector de-rating that produced the run-up is the same reaction function behind finding 4, so the evidence cuts mildly against the lean, and the scaled number (-0.36) is kept small.

lessons_applied: 'You were right about the number and too small about the move' and 'size the move on what is new': abs_move_pct raised from 4.0 to 4.5 (new numbers, not pre-released; peer print-day moves of 7.6, 5.6 and ~3-5 this fortnight); the reaction history moves p_up, not size
'A verified fact is not a predicted reaction' / this name sells its beats: the profit-beat finding cut from +0.5 to +0.3; p_up held at 46 rather than leaning up
'A narrow proxy loses...' / macro-to-company is a hypothesis: the peer-reaction finding cut from -0.7 to -0.5 and the deposits/mortgage finding from -0.3 to -0.2
'The move is in the guide': the guidance finding kept at -0.8 as the largest single item, because a reiterated guide is the base case and that was the July trigger
'Keep findings inside the window': Cetelem and the year-end guidance refinement kept in outside_window
